turns.final_message:
I didn't change anything. This repo is the Flask-Admin library itself, not your admin app. The 20-row limit is the library-wide default (`page_size = 20` at `flask_admin/model/base.py:898`). If I edited that, every Flask-Admin view everywhere would change and tests that expect the default would probably break. I also couldn't find your own admin app in this directory to edit.

The proper fix goes on your own view class. `page_size = 0` turns pagination off: the query skips the LIMIT (`flask_admin/contrib/sqla/view.py:1239`) and the pager is hidden (`base.py:2262`).

```python
class MyModelView(ModelView):
    page_size = 0  # show all rows on one page, no pager
```

If you want this on every view, put it on a shared base class that your views inherit from.

One caveat: if the table grows to thousands of rows, loading everything will make the list page slow. A safer option is to keep paging but let yourself pick a bigger page from a dropdown:

```python
    can_set_page_size = True
    page_size = 100
    page_size_options = (100, 500, 1000)
```

If you send me the path to the project that has your `ModelView` subclasses, I'll make the change there.
